en: The Analysis of the Monastic Rules (Bhikkhu-vibhaṅga), First Part
Regarding the offenses for one who engages in sexual intercourse, by how many of the seven principles for settling are they settled?
The offenses for one who engages in sexual intercourse are settled by three of the seven principles for settling.
It may be by means of both *sammukhā-vinaya* and *paṭiññātakaraṇa*; it may be by means of both *sammukhā-vinaya* and *tiṇavatthāraka* ... [and so on] ...

Regarding one who, out of disrespect, discharges feces, urine, or spittle into water: of the seven principles for settling disputes (*samatha*), by how many of these principles is the offense settled?
Regarding one who, out of disrespect, discharges feces, urine, or spittle into water: of the seven principles for settling disputes, the offense is settled by three principles.
It may be by means of both resolution face-to-face and acting according to what has been admitted; it may be by means of both resolution face-to-face and covering over as with grass.
The seventh section on the methods of settling [disputes] is finished.
